messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran a hybrid KV-cache quant bake this morning (FP8 for KV linear layers + INT8 elsewhere) on the perf harness. seeing unexpected p95 tail increases at longer sequences.

ajay: details? which model + sequence lengths? :eyes:

maria: model: rdm-13b-open-adapt (same as onboarding). batch=8, seqs=[128,512,1024]. workloads: prompt mix A (dialogs) + perf synthetic prefixes.

sasha: numbers?

maria: TL;DR table pasted below (token latency ms):

- baseline FP32: p50/p95 = 10.8 / 59.7 (seq=1024) memory=100%
- INT8-KV (quantize KV matmuls only): p50/p95 = 11.4 / 72.2 (seq=1024) memory=72%
- FP8-KV (fp8 for KV, rest FP32): p50/p95 = 9.9 / 98.4 (seq=1024) memory=64%
- HYBRID (KV FP8, attention/FC INT8+FP8 fallback heur): p50/p95 = 12.1 / 110.6 (seq=1024) memory=66%

Note: p95 jumps primarily at seq >=512. p50 improves for FP8-KV but p95 much worse.

oliver: that's surprising — FP8 lowering p95 that much. could be dequant hotpath or cache eviction cost. did you track KV cache hit rates and copy times?

maria: yes — KV hit rate stable (~98%). observed extra memcpy spikes on the NVMe->GPU path during ridge cases (bursty prefix cache loads).

kevin: also wondering about kernel selection differences. FP8 uses different matmul kernel that is more bursty with long sequences. do we have kernel-level perf logs?

maria: pasted perf gist block:

```
# perf sample (trimmed)
seq=1024, batch=8
kernel: kv_linear_fp8_gemm launch 220ms cumulative per-request (spikes)
kernel: dequantize_kv_block 14ms avg
cuda memcpy async peaks at 45ms for some requests
```

ajay: did you try keeping KV in INT8 but FP8 for weights only?

maria: yes — INT8-KV kept tail lower but memory savings worse than full FP8-KV. Hybrid was an attempt to get memory + tail, but seems we got neither.

sasha: what about cache chunking? if FP8 pack/unpack forces larger contiguous transfers -> bigger memcpy spikes. might try smaller chunk size or overlap copy+decode.

maria: good call. next run will: chunk_size=256, prefetch async=on, overlap decode thread pool=2. also will instrument kernel queue times.

ci-bot: perf-suite/kv-hybrid-1793001234 started — link: https://ci.redwood/perf/1793001234 (results in ~30m)

oliver: also add experiment where we keep prefix KV in FP32 for first 512 tokens then use FP8 for older segments (tiered precision). could avoid recent-cache spikes.

maria: adding tiered-precision test. planning matrix: baseline, int8-kv, fp8-kv, hybrid, tiered-512, chunked-256. will upload results to the perf dashboard and tag you.

kevin: capture model logits/regression eval set too — want to ensure no deg on LlamaEval-Common. put the eval run on the same seeds.

maria: yes will run eval set (200 prompts) post-perf. expecting tiny BLEU/ROUGE deltas but will watch hallucination rate.

sasha: if p95 still bad, maybe fallback policy: use FP32 for requests with seq>512, else FP8. simpler routing than hybrid kernels.

maria: noted. thanks. will post a short writeup after runs. :thumbsup:

ajay: thanks — nice writeup. ping if you want help with kernel traces.

ci-bot: perf-suite/kv-hybrid-1793001234 finished: artifacts uploaded to https://ci.redwood/perf/1793001234/artifacts (csv + flamegraphs)

maria: uploaded summary and flamegraphs to #eng-ml/perf-reports. preliminary conclusion: FP8-KV reduces memory but introduces larger memcpy+kernel tail for long contexts; mitigations to try: chunking, tiered precision, overlap copies.

oliver: good iterative plan. let's not rush rollout to dedicated until we have stable tails — set canary threshold p95 <= baseline*1.2.

maria: agreed — setting canary rule now. will update once tiered/chunked runs complete.

kevin: if any of the hybrid configs pass with p95 <=1.15x and mem savings >=30% that's a strong candidate for Dedicated config.

maria: noted — thanks all.
